settings.label: Display Mode

default.note: Chosen on first run; not a fixed default.

settings.description: Chooses whether CS2 runs in a window, in exclusive fullscreen, or in a borderless fullscreen window.
settings.tradeoffs: Behaviour differs between systems and drivers; test after changing.

settings.label: Aspect Ratio
settings.description: Sets the shape of the rendered image. Changing it changes which resolutions are listed.
settings.tradeoffs: A personal preference; narrower ratios show less of the scene horizontally.

settings.label: Resolution
settings.description: Sets the rendering resolution. Lower resolutions reduce GPU work but make the image less sharp.
settings.tradeoffs: The list depends on the display and aspect ratio; options here are simulated for a 1920x1080 display.
settings.verificationNotes: Label verified in game files; options are populated at runtime from the display, so this list is simulated.

settings.label: Refresh Rate
settings.description: Sets the display refresh rate used in fullscreen modes.
settings.tradeoffs: Only rates supported by the display are listed; options here are simulated for a 144 Hz display.

hints.why: Using the display's highest supported refresh rate lets it show more of the frames the game renders.

settings.verificationNotes: Label verified in game files; options are populated at runtime, so this list is simulated.

settings.label: Boost Player Contrast

default.note: r_player_visibility_mode registers default 1; the layout does not name this control's convar.

settings.description: Improves the legibility of players in low contrast situations. Enabling Boost Player Contrast can degrade graphics performance.
settings.tradeoffs: Valve notes it can degrade graphics performance.

hints.why: Valve describes it as improving the legibility of players in low contrast situations.
Valve notes that enabling it can degrade graphics performance.

settings.label: V-Sync

default.note: Stored in the video config, not a convar.

settings.description: V-Sync helps ensure the game's frame rate matches the display's refresh rate, usually resulting in a smoother visual experience that eliminates screen tearing.
settings.tradeoffs: Disabling it can reintroduce screen tearing. Synchronising to the display can add input delay on some systems; the size of the effect depends on hardware.

hints.why: Waiting for the display refresh can add input delay on some systems; turning V-Sync off removes that wait at the cost of possible tearing.
Valve's tooltip says V-Sync eliminates screen tearing.

settings.label: NVIDIA G-Sync

availability.note: Only available on certain displays; enabled outside the game in the NVIDIA Control Panel.

settings.description: NVIDIA G-Sync allows a display to dynamically change its refresh rate to match the game's frame rate where possible, resulting in a smoother visual experience. It is only available on certain displays.
settings.tradeoffs: Requires a compatible display and driver configuration outside the game.

settings.label: NVIDIA Reflex Low Latency
settings.description: NVIDIA Reflex is used to reduce system latency which increases PC responsiveness. Boost mode includes techniques that may draw more power to the GPU and slightly impact FPS to reduce latency as much as possible.
settings.tradeoffs: Boost may draw more GPU power and slightly reduce FPS (per Valve's tooltip).

hints.why: Valve's tooltip says Reflex reduces system latency and increases PC responsiveness.

settings.label: Maximum FPS In Game

default.note: fps_max registers default 120 in build 2000948 (0 means no limit, which this slider cannot show).

settings.description: Set an upper limit for the frame rate you can experience while playing the game.
settings.tradeoffs: A lower cap can reduce heat and power use; a cap below what your PC can render limits smoothness.

settings.label: Current Video Values Preset

default.note: CS2 picks a preset for the detected hardware.

settings.description: Applies one of CS2's four video presets to the eleven quality settings below. It shows Custom when the current values do not match a preset.
settings.tradeoffs: Changing the preset overwrites the individual quality settings listed below it.
settings.verificationNotes: Preset contents taken from video_defaults_0..3.txt in build 2000948.

settings.label: Multisampling Anti-Aliasing Mode

default.note: Set by the autodetected preset (High preset: 4x MSAA).

settings.description: Anti-aliasing provides a smooth appearance at the edges of geometry, eliminating jagged edges. Increasing anti-aliasing quality can degrade graphics performance.
settings.tradeoffs: Higher sample counts cost more GPU time; lower settings show more jagged edges.

hints.why: Valve notes that increasing anti-aliasing quality can degrade graphics performance, so a lower mode may help if the GPU is the bottleneck.
Higher anti-aliasing smooths jagged edges.

settings.verificationNotes: Option labels verified in localization; the client populates their order at runtime, so the order shown here is not verified.

settings.label: Global Shadow Quality
settings.description: Sets the overall quality of shadows.
settings.tradeoffs: Higher shadow quality generally costs more GPU time; the exact effect is hardware dependent.

hints.why: Shadow rendering is commonly one of the more expensive effects; a step down may reduce GPU load (no Valve-published measurement).

settings.label: Dynamic Shadows
settings.description: Select the light sources for which dynamic objects such as players and smoke cast shadows. "Sun Only" can improve graphics performance but might leave you at a competitive disadvantage, particularly indoors.
settings.tradeoffs: "Sun Only" can improve performance but might leave you at a competitive disadvantage, particularly indoors (Valve).

hints.why: Valve warns that "Sun Only" might leave you at a competitive disadvantage, particularly indoors, because fewer light sources cast player shadows.
Valve says "Sun Only" can improve graphics performance.

settings.label: Model / Texture Detail
settings.description: The model / texture detail setting controls the resolution of textures and geometric complexity of models in the game. Decreasing this setting may improve performance on low-end systems, but will degrade image quality.
settings.tradeoffs: Lower detail may improve performance on low-end systems but degrades image quality (Valve).

hints.why: Valve says decreasing it may improve performance on low-end systems.

settings.label: Texture Filtering Mode
settings.description: Increasing the texture filtering setting improves the appearance of textures in the game. Increasing filtering quality can degrade graphics performance.
settings.tradeoffs: Higher filtering looks sharper at angles but can cost performance (Valve).

hints.why: Valve notes that increasing filtering quality can degrade graphics performance.

settings.label: Shader Detail
settings.description: Shader detail controls the sophistication of the lighting and shading effects applied to surfaces in the game. Higher settings increase visual quality but can degrade graphics performance.
settings.tradeoffs: High looks better but can degrade performance (Valve).

hints.why: Valve notes higher shader detail can degrade graphics performance.

settings.label: Particle Detail
settings.description: Particle detail controls the complexity of particle effects and whether particles cast shadows. Higher settings increase visual quality but can degrade graphics performance.
settings.tradeoffs: Higher detail can degrade performance, especially in effect-heavy moments (Valve).

hints.why: Valve notes higher particle detail can degrade graphics performance.

settings.label: Ambient Occlusion
settings.description: Calculate lighting using Ambient Occlusion. Enabling Ambient Occlusion can degrade graphics performance.
settings.tradeoffs: Adds contact shading but can degrade performance (Valve).

hints.why: Valve notes enabling Ambient Occlusion can degrade graphics performance.

settings.label: Parallax Occlusion Mapping
settings.description: Gives some surfaces, such as snow, real looking depth. Enabling it can degrade graphics performance.
settings.tradeoffs: Adds surface depth but can degrade performance (Valve).

hints.why: Valve notes enabling it can degrade graphics performance.

settings.label: High Dynamic Range
settings.description: High Dynamic Range (HDR) controls the range of brightness between the brightest and darkest pixels. Choosing Performance decreases the quality of HDR rendering but potentially increases performance and reduces GPU memory use.
settings.tradeoffs: Performance mode lowers HDR quality but may increase performance and reduce GPU memory use (Valve).

hints.why: Valve says Performance potentially increases performance and reduces GPU memory use.

settings.label: FidelityFX Super Resolution
settings.description: FidelityFX Super Resolution may improve performance by rendering at reduced resolution and upscaling using a high-quality spatial technique.
settings.tradeoffs: Upscaling from a lower resolution can soften fine detail, which may make distant targets harder to read.

hints.why: Valve says FSR may improve performance by rendering at reduced resolution and upscaling.
Rendering at native resolution avoids upscaling softness that can affect small, distant details.

subtabs.label: HUD Edge Positions
subtabs.note: Opens an on-screen positioning tool in CS2; not simulated.

settings.label: Master Volume
settings.description: Overall game volume.

settings.label: Main Menu Ambience Volume
settings.description: Volume of background sounds in the main menu.

settings.label: Audio Device
settings.description: Controls which audio device Counter-Strike uses.
settings.verificationNotes: Label and tooltip verified; device names are simulated.

settings.label: EQ Profile

default.note: Tooltip also marks Natural as default.

settings.description: Changes overall sound coloration in CS2. Natural (default) adds no coloration; Crisp enhances mid and high frequency bands and can help with sound localization; Smooth reduces harshness.
settings.tradeoffs: Valve: Crisp "may sound harsh in certain situations"; give yourself time to acclimate to a new EQ profile.

hints.why: Valve's tooltip says Crisp enhances mid and high frequencies and can help with sound localization and reduce muffling.

settings.label: L/R Isolation
settings.description: 0% is physically modelled panning (default). 100% hard-pans emitters directly to the side, giving a strong sense of left vs right.
settings.tradeoffs: Valve: strong isolation "can be positionally misleading at certain angles".

settings.label: Perspective Correction

default.note: Tooltip says 'Yes (default)'; the convar dump registers false.

settings.description: Yes: sound sources are rendered accurately with respect to your field of view on screen. No: emitters at the edge of the field of view are rendered without that correction.

settings.label: Play Audio When Game In Background
settings.description: Whether game audio keeps playing when CS2 is not the focused window.

settings.label: Other Player Voice Volume
settings.description: Adjusts overall volume of incoming voice communications from other players (VOIP).

settings.label: Voice/Microphone Mode
settings.description: Disables your microphone, transmits only while the push-to-talk key is held, or transmits whenever your voice exceeds the trigger threshold.

hints.why: Voice must be enabled for teammates to hear you.

settings.label: Voice Input Audio Device
settings.description: Controls which audio device Counter-Strike uses for microphone voice capture.

settings.label: Hear My Own Voice
settings.description: Turn this on to listen to your microphone while adjusting audio settings.

settings.label: Streamlined Push To Talk
settings.description: Open recording device when the game starts, instead of the first time the mic is used.

settings.label: Master Music Volume
settings.description: Overall music volume. Scales every music volume below it, for every game mode.

settings.label: Music Volumes For
settings.description: Each game mode keeps its own set of music volumes. Pick a mode here to see and change the volumes used while you are playing it - your other modes are left alone.
settings.verificationNotes: Per-mode music volumes were added on 2026-09-22. Only the Competitive set is simulated.

settings.label: Main Menu Volume
settings.description: Main menu background, loading screen, match found, team select, team intro, end of match, music kit preview.

settings.label: Round Start Volume
settings.description: Music during buy time.

settings.label: Round End Volume
settings.description: Music when your team loses or wins a round.

settings.label: Ten Second Warning Volume
settings.description: Upon last ten seconds of the bomb countdown, the round ending, or hostage carrier approaching a rescue zone.

settings.label: Death Camera Volume
settings.description: Music upon death.

settings.label: Mute MVP Music when players on both teams are alive
settings.description: If set, MVP music is muted if players from both teams are still alive.

hints.why: Valve's description: MVP music is muted while players from both teams are still alive, leaving the soundscape clearer.

settings.label: Competitive EQ
settings.description: Applies this EQ profile for the duration of a Competitive match.
settings.tradeoffs: Crisp may sound harsh in certain situations (Valve, EQ Profile tooltip).

hints.why: Valve's EQ tooltip says Crisp can help with sound localization and reduce muffling.

settings.label: Casual EQ
settings.description: Applies this EQ profile for the duration of a Casual match.

settings.label: Deathmatch EQ
settings.description: Applies this EQ profile for the duration of Deathmatch.

settings.label: Arms Race EQ
settings.description: Applies this EQ profile for the duration of Arms Race.

settings.label: Enable Developer Console
settings.description: Allows the developer console to be opened. Launch options like -dev or -console override this setting.

settings.label: Max Acceptable Matchmaking Ping
settings.description: Specifies the maximum acceptable ping when official matchmaking searches for a server; if no nearby server satisfies it, you may be placed on the nearest available one.
settings.tradeoffs: A very low limit can lengthen queue times.

settings.label: Max Acceptable Game Traffic Bandwidth

default.note: The registered convar default (80000) is not one of the menu options.

settings.description: Sets how much game traffic servers send you. A lower rate can help avoid packet loss on restrictive connections, but too little bandwidth can delay updates when many players are active.
settings.tradeoffs: Insufficient bandwidth can result in delayed network packets (Valve).

settings.label: Buffering to smooth over packet loss / jitter
settings.description: Buffer snapshots from the server and commands from the client. This reduces the rate of missed ticks but increases your effective ping time.
settings.tradeoffs: Fewer missed ticks on unstable connections, but higher effective ping (Valve).

hints.why: Valve says buffering reduces the rate of missed ticks caused by packet loss or jitter.
Valve says buffering increases your effective ping time.

settings.label: CPU Cores Usage Preference
settings.description: Some CPUs have cores designed for high performance and others for power efficiency. This configures whether work is preferentially assigned to one or the other type of core. Requires a game restart.
settings.tradeoffs: Valve: the best setting will vary depending on your hardware and software configuration.

settings.label: HUD Scale
settings.description: HUD Scale adjusts the size of all HUD elements.

settings.label: HUD Color
settings.description: This color is applied to selected parts of the HUD, including health, armor and ammo.

settings.label: Large Player Count
settings.description: During the active portion of the round, replace player avatars with team player count in the mini-scoreboard.

hints.why: Shows a single large alive-count instead of avatars, a simpler read of the round state.

settings.label: Glow Weapon with Rarity Color
settings.description: Colors the weapon selection HUD with each item's rarity color (added 2025-05-13).

settings.label: Show Team ID Through Walls
settings.description: How much teammate information is shown over teammates, including through walls.
settings.tradeoffs: More information is more visual clutter on screen.

settings.label: Show Player Colors in Competitive
settings.description: In competitive, shows teammates as separate colors on the radar, scoreboard and elsewhere; 'Colors and Letters' adds a letter to each color.

hints.why: Adding letters to teammate colors does not rely on color perception alone.

settings.label: Player Pings
settings.description: Controls whether teammates' location pings are shown, and whether they play a sound.

settings.label: Mute Enemy Team
settings.description: Block all communication from players on the enemy team.

hints.why: Blocks enemy-team chat and voice, which removes one source of distraction.

settings.label: Mute All But Friends
settings.description: Block communication from everyone except players you are friends with or players in your matchmaking party.
settings.tradeoffs: You will not hear callouts from teammates who are not friends or in your party.

settings.label: Clean Player Names
settings.description: Change names of players not on your friends list to something neutral.

settings.label: Smooth Spectator Camera
settings.description: Sets whether your spectator camera will smoothly interpolate to the next target when switching between players.

settings.label: Viewmodel Position
settings.description: Chooses a preset position for the first-person weapon model.
settings.tradeoffs: A personal preference; it changes how much of the screen the weapon covers.

settings.label: Preferred Viewmodel Left/Right Handedness
settings.description: Set the default viewmodel left/right handedness. There is also a key binding to switch hands temporarily during gameplay.

settings.label: First Person Tracers
settings.description: Whether or not to render your own bullet tracers locally. Other players will still see them.

settings.label: Always Show Inventory
settings.description: Keeps your current loadout visible on the HUD.

settings.label: Open Buy Menu With Use Key
settings.description: Pressing the Use key opens the buy menu when you are in a buy zone.

settings.label: Radar Centers The Player
settings.description: Toggles between a radar that is centered around the player or best fit.

settings.label: Radar Is Rotating
settings.description: Toggles between a radar that rotates and a radar with a fixed orientation.

settings.label: Radar Hud Size
settings.description: Adjusts the size of the radar relative to other Hud elements.

settings.label: Radar Map Zoom
settings.description: Map Zoom impacts the amount of the map that is visible on the radar.

settings.label: Toggle Square Shape With Scoreboard
settings.description: If set to Yes, the radar will toggle to square and display the whole map when the scoreboard is visible.

settings.label: Radar Is Zooming Dynamically
settings.description: Toggles between a radar that scales dynamically to encompass all detected elements and one with fixed scale.

hints.why: A dynamic radar grows to include teammates, the bomb and detected enemies.

settings.label: Predict Body Shot Effects
settings.description: Predict the audio/visual effects of body shots such as blood spurts and sound effects.
settings.tradeoffs: Effects appear before the server confirms the hit, so occasionally a predicted hit will not have counted.

hints.why: Shows hit feedback immediately instead of waiting for the server round trip (a perceived-responsiveness change, not a change to actual latency).

settings.label: Predict Head Shot Effects
settings.description: Predict the audio/visual effects of head shots such as sparks and dink sounds.
settings.tradeoffs: Effects appear before the server confirms the hit, so occasionally a predicted hit will not have counted.

settings.label: Predict Kill Ragdolls
settings.description: Targets immediately ragdoll when a kill is predicted. If the prediction turns out to be wrong, the target snaps back to its server-authoritative position.

settings.label: Show frame time and FPS
settings.description: Shows the worst recent frame time in milliseconds, and the current average frames per second.

hints.why: Showing frame time and FPS lets you measure whether other changes actually help on your machine.

settings.label: Show ping
settings.description: Shows the round trip latency to the server, in milliseconds.

hints.why: Lets you see whether latency problems come from the network.

settings.label: Show network problems (ticks missed due to loss / jitter)
settings.description: Shows the percentage of ticks that are not available at the time they are needed, due to network loss or late delivery.

hints.why: Makes packet loss and jitter visible, so you can tell whether buffering would help.

settings.label: Reverse Mouse

default.note: Default analog binding maps MOUSE_Y to pitch (not inverted).

settings.description: Inverts vertical mouse look.

settings.label: Duck Mode
settings.description: Whether crouching requires holding the key or toggles on each press.

hints.why: Toggle avoids holding a key for long periods.

settings.label: Walk Mode
settings.description: Whether walking requires holding the key or toggles on each press.

hints.why: Toggle avoids holding a key for long periods.

settings.label: Silent Reload Mode
settings.description: With Toggle, once a silent reload starts you can let go of the reload button; tapping reload again cancels back to a fast reload (added 2026-10-28).

hints.why: Valve added Toggle so you do not need to hold the key through the slower silent reload.

settings.label: Zoom Button Hold
settings.description: Whether or not holding the zoom button should behave as if it was pressed repeatedly.

settings.label: Mouse Sensitivity
settings.description: Mouse sensitivity for aiming.
settings.tradeoffs: Personal aim preference. Values are not comparable with other games' sensitivity scales, so the assistant never proposes a number.

settings.label: Zoom Sensitivity Multiplier
settings.description: Additional mouse sensitivity scale factor applied when the field of view is zoomed in.
settings.tradeoffs: Personal aim preference; the assistant never proposes a number.

settings.label: Move Forward
settings.description: Key bound to +forward.

settings.label: Move Backward
settings.description: Key bound to +back.

settings.label: Move Left (strafe)
settings.description: Key bound to +left.

settings.label: Move Right (strafe)
settings.description: Key bound to +right.

settings.label: Walk
settings.description: Key bound to +sprint (walk quietly).

settings.label: Duck
settings.description: Key bound to +duck.

settings.label: Jump
settings.description: Key bound to +jump.

settings.label: Use
settings.description: Key bound to +use.

settings.label: Reload
settings.description: Key bound to +reload. Holding it performs a silent reload (2026-09-22 update).

settings.label: Drop Weapon
settings.description: Key bound to drop.

settings.label: Inspect Weapon
settings.description: Key bound to +lookatweapon.

settings.label: Buy Menu
settings.description: Key bound to buymenu.

settings.label: Scoreboard
settings.description: Key bound to +showscores.

settings.label: Toggle Radar Zoom

default.note: Not bound in the default key file.

settings.description: Toggles between Radar Map Zoom and Radar Map Alternate Zoom.

settings.label: Toggle Console
settings.description: Key bound to toggleconsole (requires Enable Developer Console).

settings.label: Player Ping
settings.description: Key bound to player_ping.

settings.label: Use Microphone
settings.description: Push-to-talk key (+voicerecord).

settings.label: Temporarily Disable Incoming Chat

default.note: Not bound in the default key file.

settings.description: Disable voice chat until the end of the round. Useful for temporarily muting noisy teammates when you need to hear clearly. A 'Clutch Key'.

settings.label: Style

default.note: Matches the 2026-09-22 note: default updated to "Dynamic Quad".

settings.description: Crosshair shape. Dynamic styles show the real weapon spread and inaccuracy; static styles keep a fixed shape.
settings.tradeoffs: Dynamic styles communicate accuracy but move; static styles are steadier but do not show spread.

settings.label: Outline
settings.description: Draw a black outline around the crosshair for better visibility. Half Outline draws only the top-left portions of the outline.

hints.why: Valve's description: the outline is drawn "for better visibility" against bright backgrounds.

settings.label: Thickness
settings.description: Thickness of the crosshair bars in pixels (since 2026-09-23 the unit is pixels and rescales with resolution changes).

settings.label: Center Dot
settings.description: Draw a dot at the center of the crosshair.

settings.label: Length
settings.description: Length of each crosshair bar in pixels.

settings.label: Gap
settings.description: Gap between the crosshair center and the bars, in pixels.
settings.verificationNotes: The layout uses 0-128 for most styles and -10 to 128 for the classic dynamic style; only the 0-128 range is simulated.

settings.label: Dynamic Spread Limit
settings.description: Limits how far the dynamic crosshair spreads at maximum inaccuracy, beyond a baseline spread distance.

settings.label: T Style
settings.description: T-style crosshair: hide the top bar.

settings.label: Use crosshair color for scope dot
settings.description: Should the scope dot match the user's crosshair color.

settings.label: Scope dot scale
settings.description: Scale of the scope dot on weapons with a dot scope.

settings.label: Follow Recoil
settings.description: Crosshair follows the weapon's predicted recoil (aim punch).

settings.label: Friendly Fire Reticle Warning
settings.description: Changes the reticle to warn you when a teammate is under your crosshair.

settings.label: Show Player Crosshairs
settings.description: Show the crosshair of other players while spectating.

settings.label: Keep Regular Crosshair
settings.description: Keep the regular crosshair visible when the grenade line-up reticle is shown.

settings.label: Delay Sniper Rifle Un-Scope after Shot
settings.description: Delays the automatic un-scope after a sniper rifle shot.

settings.label: Show Scoped Sniper Rifle Inaccuracy
settings.description: Shows weapon inaccuracy inside sniper scopes (added 2025-10-01).

settings.label: Auto Re-Zoom Sniper Rifle after Shot
settings.description: Auto-rezoom snipers after a shot.

settings.label: Sniper crosshair thickness
settings.description: If greater than 1, sniper scope cross lines gain extra width (1 is a single-pixel hairline).
